land.text: the republic of the Convention, Belgium and the occupied left bank of the Rhine included

predecessors.note: 'The Directory governed the French First Republic from 26 October 1795 (4 Brumaire an IV)'; the First Republic page of the same dossier set gives 3 November 1795. Cliopatria's Directory row starts in 1796.

land.text: the whole republic after the coup of 18 Brumaire (9-10 November 1799)

capitals.name: Paris
capitals.note: Infobox 'Seat: Luxembourg Palace, Paris'; the page has no separate capital field.

correction.text: the republic as the Convention left it, taken over by the Directory on 26 October 1795

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1795: the page opens the Directory on 26 October 1795 and Cliopatria's Directory shape begins only in 1796, so the last two months of 1795 take the First Republic's 1795 shape unchanged.

685,238 km2 for 1796, colonies included. The Italian cells (Lombardy 62, Piedmont 31, Emilia 19, Liguria 17, Veneto 10) are lands the French army held in the campaign of 1796, not French territory: the ledger carries Lombardy (after Lodi, 10 May 1796) and the Piedmont fortresses (Cherasco, 28 April 1796) as occupations; the page does not mention Emilia, Liguria or the Veneto, which stay a gap (notes). Corsica is correctly out until the British left on 11 October 1796. The Directory page gives no area to compare.

655,673 km2 for 1797-1798. Belgium, the Rhineland (annexed by Campo Formio, 17 October 1797), Savoy, Nice, Corsica and Corfu (one cell, the Ionian Islands 'gained from Venice' in October 1797) are in; the 29 Italian cells (Piedmont west, western Liguria) are the fringe of the 1796 armistice and the county of Nice that the pages do not delineate. Geneva (two cells) is drawn French from 1796, but the page dates its union to 26 August 1798; kept, a few cells.

752,853 km2 for 1799. Egypt (200 cells, 50,580 km2, from 'Alexandria was captured on 2 July 1798'), Malta, Corfu and Piedmont (101 cells, occupied from 6 December 1798) are in. Egypt and Piedmont are occupations or conquests the ledger dates, not annexations; the 10 added Savoy cells and the Swiss cells (Geneva's surroundings and others) are not explained by any opened page. Naples (the Parthenopean Republic, 26 January 1799) is a client, three Campanian cells at most. The page gives no area.

region.text: the French Republic as the Convention left it

ledger.note: 26 October 1795: the Directory takes over the Republic. 'The Directory governed the French First Republic from 26 October 1795 (4 Brumaire an IV)'; infobox 'Formation: 26/31 October 1795'; the directors were chosen on 31 October.

region.text: the Netherlands of the Batavian Republic

ledger.note: The Batavian Republic stays France's sister republic. 'It was proclaimed on 19 January 1795'; status 'Sister republic of the French First Republic and First French Empire'; relation carried over from french-first-republic.

region.text: the left bank of the Rhine

ledger.note: The left bank of the Rhine stays in French hands. 'The Treaty of Basel ... recognized France's occupation of the left bank of the Rhine'; relation carried over from french-first-republic until Campo Formio (October 1797). [Reviewer eu-20-a, 2026-10-31: region narrowed to the left bank: the gazetteer's Rhineland includes all of Nordrhein-Westfalen and the right bank; intersected with Cliopatria's French First Republic 1794 shape.]

region.text: the Piedmont cells of the 1796 shape, the districts held under the armistice

ledger.note: 28 April 1796: Sardinia is knocked out of the war. 'Sardinia was forced to accept the Armistice of Cherasco on 28 April, knocking it out of the war and the First Coalition.' The page does not say which places the French garrisoned; the region is the Piedmont cells of Cliopatria's 1796 shape.

region.text: Lombardy, after the battle of Lodi (10 May 1796)

ledger.note: 10 May 1796: Lombardy falls to Bonaparte. 'the Austrian army of General Beaulieu was defeated in the Battle of Lodi on 10 May'; the Cisalpine page: 'After the Battle of Lodi (May 1796), Napoleon set up two states, one on each side of the Po'. The page has no sentence on Milan.

region.text: Corsica, retaken after the British evacuation

ledger.note: October 1796: France retakes Corsica. 'British evacuation: 11 October 1796'; 'On 19 October 1796, the French reconquered Bastia.'

region.text: Lombardy, now the core of the Cisalpine Republic

ledger.note: 29 June 1797: Lombardy becomes the Cisalpine Republic. Infobox 'Established: 29 June 1797', 'Sister Republic of France'; the occupation of 1796 turns into a client state.

region.text: the Cisalpine Republic

ledger.note: 29 June 1797: the Cisalpine Republic, a sister republic of France, is decreed at Milan. Infobox 'Status: Sister Republic of France', 'Established: 29 June 1797'; 'on 12 Messidor (29 June), he decreed the birth of the Cisalpine Republic'.

region.text: the Ligurian Republic

ledger.note: 14 June 1797: the Ligurian Republic is founded under French oversight. Infobox 'Status: sister republic of France'; 'formed by Napoleon on 14 June 1797'. Cliopatria draws its Genoese core only.

region.text: the left bank of the Rhine, recognised at Campo Formio

ledger.note: 17 October 1797: the Treaty of Campo Formio gives France the left bank of the Rhine. 'On 17 October 1797, General Bonaparte and the Austrians signed the Treaty of Campoformio.' France gained 'the left bank of the Rhine, Belgium and the Ionian Islands'; the territorial-evolution page lists 'The German states on the left bank of the Rhine (1797)'. [Reviewer eu-20-a, 2026-10-31: region narrowed to the left bank: the gazetteer's Rhineland includes all of Nordrhein-Westfalen and the right bank; intersected with Cliopatria's French First Republic 1794 shape.]

region.text: the left bank of the Rhine, France's by Campo Formio

ledger.note: 17 October 1797: the left bank of the Rhine is annexed. France received it under the Treaty of Campo Formio; Belgium (annexed since 1 October 1795) is recognised in the same treaty, and Austria 'relinquished its claim' there. [Reviewer eu-20-a, 2026-10-31: region narrowed to the left bank: the gazetteer's Rhineland includes all of Nordrhein-Westfalen and the right bank; intersected with Cliopatria's French Directory 1797 shape. Confidence 3 -> 2: the page reads 'France received the left bank of the Rhine as far south as Andernach', not the whole left bank.]

region.text: the Ionian Islands, gained from Venice under Campo Formio

ledger.note: October 1797: the Ionian Islands pass from Venice to France. The page: France gained 'the Ionian Islands' under Campo Formio, 17 October 1797 ('gained from Venice').

region.text: Mulhouse, which 'had voted in favour of its reunion to France in 1798'

ledger.note: 1798: Mulhouse joins France. The page: Mulhouse 'had voted in favour of its reunion to France in 1798'; no month.

region.text: Malta, taken during the Egyptian expedition of 1798

ledger.note: 1798: Malta is taken. The fleet that sailed on 19 May 1798 'took the island' on the way to Egypt; the page gives no date for Malta.

region.text: Rome and its state, the Roman Republic

ledger.note: 10 February 1798: the Roman Republic is proclaimed after Berthier occupies Rome. 'Thus the Roman Republic was also proclaimed on 10 February 1798.' A French client state.

region.text: the Helvetic Republic

ledger.note: 12 April 1798: the Helvetic Republic is proclaimed. 'was proclaimed on 12 April 1798.' A French client state; the Swiss Confederation row ends in 1798 in Cliopatria.

region.text: Egypt, entered at Alexandria on 2 July 1798

ledger.note: 2 July 1798: Bonaparte takes Alexandria and, with Egypt, the Nile valley. 'Alexandria was captured on 2 July 1798' after the fleet 'sailed on 19 May 1798'; the Battle of the Pyramids (21 July 1798) is not on the page. Held as a conquest, not annexed, until 1801.

region.text: Geneva, made part of France

ledger.note: 26 August 1798: Geneva is made part of France. 'On 26 August 1798, Geneva was detached from the new republic and made part of France'; the territorial-evolution page lists 'The Republic of Geneva (1798)'.

region.text: the Piedmont cells held since the 1796 armistice

ledger.note: December 1798: the armistice districts merge into the occupation of all Piedmont (bridging; the page gives no return of the 1796 districts).

region.text: Piedmont, from which the king was forced out

ledger.note: 6 December 1798: the French drive the king out of Piedmont. 'on 6 December 1798, French soldiers forced King Charles Emmanuel IV out of Piedmont'; the Piedmontese Republic was set up under French control.

region.text: Piedmont, where Suvorov restored the king

ledger.note: 1799: the French lose Piedmont. Suvorov 'soon occupied Turin and proclaimed the restoration of Piedmont to its king' after the failed Allied attack on the Po of 11 May; no month for Turin on the page.

region.text: Naples and its kingdom, the Parthenopean Republic

ledger.note: 26 January 1799: the Parthenopean Republic is proclaimed at Naples. 'on 26 January' 1799, three days after Naples was occupied on 23 January 1799. A French client state.

region.text: the Cisalpine Republic, occupied

ledger.note: 27 April 1799: the Austro-Russian army takes the Cisalpine Republic. Infobox 'Occupied by Austria: 27 April 1799'; 'the French defeats at Lecco and Cassano on 26-28 April were followed by withdrawal from Lombardy' (Italian campaigns page).

region.text: Rome and its state

ledger.note: Summer 1799: the Roman Republic collapses. After Joubert's defeat at Novi (15 August 1799) 'the Sister Republics in Italy then collapsed, leaving only Genoa under French control'; the page gives no date for Rome itself.

region.text: Naples and its kingdom

ledger.note: Summer 1799: the Parthenopean Republic collapses with the other Italian sister republics after Novi (15 August 1799); the page gives no date for Naples.

region.text: the republic, with Egypt and the sister republics still beyond its borders

ledger.note: 9 November 1799: the coup of 18 Brumaire ends the Directory. Infobox 'Abolished: 9 November 1799'; 'a parliamentary coup d'etat on 9-10 November 1799'; 'Succession: Executive Consulate'.

wars.name: War of the First Coalition (Directory years)

zones.text: the left bank of the Rhine

wars.outcome: Treaty of Basel with Prussia (5 April 1795) and Spain (22 July 1795); Bonaparte's Italian campaign, Cherasco (28 April 1796), Lodi (10 May 1796), Campo Formio (17 October 1797), which gave France the left bank of the Rhine, Belgium and the Ionian Islands.

wars.name: Anglo-Corsican Kingdom and the recovery of Corsica
wars.outcome: British evacuation on 11 October 1796; the French reconquered Bastia on 19 October 1796.
wars.note: The loss is recorded in french-first-republic (June 1794).

wars.name: French invasion of Egypt
wars.outcome: The fleet sailed on 19 May 1798, took Malta and captured Alexandria on 2 July 1798; the expedition stays in Egypt after the Directory (to 1801).
wars.note: The page does not name the Mamluk beys; the opponent is taken from the mamluk-beys-of-egypt dossier, whose ledger records the loss of Cairo to the Directory in July 1798. The British and Ottoman phase of 1801 belongs to the Consulate.

wars.name: War of the Second Coalition
wars.outcome: 'The war began on 29 November 1798' (the page's wording); Jourdan defeated at Ostrach and Stockach (25 March 1799), Moreau at Cassano (27 April 1799), Joubert at Novi (15 August 1799), after which the Italian sister republics collapsed; Italian campaigns page: Cassano 26-28 April, Novi '9 August'.
wars.note: The Directory page and the Italian campaigns page disagree on the date of Novi (15 against 9 August 1799).

certainty.note: Metropolitan France and the annexed Belgium are administrative lines; the Rhineland (sharp only from Campo Formio, 17 October 1797), the Italian occupations, the Armistice of Cherasco districts and Egypt are fronts or garrisons and soft.

notes: Cliopatria row 'French Directory' 1796..1799 (three shapes). The Directory started on 26 October 1795 (its page), so the dossier starts in 1795 with a new keyframe; the First Republic dossier ends on 3 November 1795 (its page): the 1795 overlap is two months, and the two pages differ by a week. The Wikipedia page treats Convention, Directory and Consulate as one republic; Cliopatria and this project keep three dossiers in colour family 'france'. Page budget 1-2 pages: exceeded (Directory, Italian campaigns, plus the pages shared with french-first-republic, batavian-republic, cisalpine-republic and ligurian-republic). Gaps (page silent): what the 1796 shape's Emilia (19 cells), Liguria (17) and Veneto (10) cells are (no opened page mentions Modena, Parma, Bologna or Venice's terraferma; the Venice dossier says the French held the Venetian state to the Adige by the end of 1796); the 1797-1799 Savoy and Swiss cells (possibly Geneva's hinterland or the Basel bishopric; no opened page says); the western Riviera and Oneglia; Naples as an occupation; Egypt's end in 1801 (Consulate); Belgium's formal annexation (1 October 1795) is in french-first-republic. Client states: vassal_start events for the sister republics (Batavian, Ligurian, Helvetic) have no end because they last beyond this dossier. Counterparts without a dossier at the time of writing: republic-of-mulhouse, republic-of-geneva, order-of-saint-john (Malta), parthenopean-republic; helvetic-republic and revolutionary-roman-republic are written by other parts of eu-20. The Directory page's own wording is odd in places (the Batavian Republic 'installed in 1798', the Cisalpine Republic 'created in Milan in 1798', Geneva 'detached from the new republic' on 26 August 1798); quoted where used and not corrected from memory.
